events.title: Harold Godwinson Is Crowned King of England
events.description: The day after Edward the Confessor died, England's council of nobles, the Witan, confirmed Harold Godwinson as king. He was crowned the same day, with no delay.
events.significance: Harold's rapid accession set off a succession dispute. It ended with the Norman conquest of England later that year.

events.title: Joan of Arc Is Born
events.description: Joan of Arc is traditionally said to have been born on this day, to a peasant family in the village of Domrémy in northeastern France. Historians say the date is approximate.
events.significance: As a teenager she led French forces to key victories in the Hundred Years' War. She later became a national heroine and a Catholic saint.

events.title: Samuel Morse Demonstrates the Telegraph
events.description: Samuel Morse gave the first public demonstration of his telegraph system at the Speedwell Iron Works in Morristown, New Jersey.
events.significance: The telegraph made rapid long-distance communication possible, and Morse code became a standard way of sending messages.

events.title: Alfred Wegener Presents Continental Drift
events.description: German scientist Alfred Wegener first presented his hypothesis to the German Geological Society in Frankfurt. He proposed that the continents were once joined and have slowly drifted apart.
events.significance: Many scientists rejected the idea at first. It later became a foundation of plate tectonics, which is central to modern geology.

events.title: Attack on the U.S. Capitol
events.description: A crowd of supporters of President Donald Trump stormed the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. They were trying to stop Congress from certifying the 2020 presidential election results.
events.significance: The attack disrupted the peaceful transfer of power for the first time in modern American history. It led to investigations, prosecutions, and ongoing national debate.
